brief:
Israel's president said Wednesday he hopes to avoid a second election after voting produced no clear winner, Al-Monitor reported. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and opposition leaders are now scrambling to secure coalition options, with Israeli Arab parties potentially positioned as kingmakers in government formation.

The inconclusive result leaves the country facing extended coalition negotiations rather than an immediate return to polls. Both major political blocs lack the seats needed to govern alone without support from smaller parties.
dek: Israel's president voiced hope Wednesday for avoiding a second election after a hard-fought vote produced no clear winner, leaving Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and the opposition scrambling for options and making Israeli Arab parties possible kingmakers.
title: Israel's president urges against new election after inconclusive vote
